_comment: A23 (§13.5). The mutation half of the gate: 'a suite that kills mutants is the only proof the tests are real'. Scope mirrors vitest.config.ts's coverage `include`/`exclude` exactly, so the two halves of the gate measure the same files.
_disableTypeChecks_comment: S5 layer 2. Stryker's default is `true`, which prepends `// @ts-nocheck` to every JavaScript-and-friends file it copies into the sandbox — including `public/ocr/`, four vendored files of the self-hosted OCR engine. Sixteen bytes into `tesseract.esm.min.js` is sixteen bytes the digest in `assets.generated.ts` does not describe, so every asset assertion fails in the dry run and no mutation score can be produced for anything. Measured: `tesseract.esm.min.js: expected 63220 bytes, got 63236`. The pattern below is the projects own source, which is all Stryker ever instruments.
_ignoreComment: TA6/SB-9 (§13.5). `ignorePatterns` keeps build output and fixtures out of the sandbox and nothing else: no file under src/ belongs here. Excluding a test file does not exclude the source it covers, so every such entry scores that source with its own test switched off and reports the survivors as gaps. src/lib/storage/db.test.ts was listed while it moved the clock with process.env.TZ, which is inert under the `threads` pool Stryker's vitest runner pins; A23-a replaced that with a stubbed Date, the file passes under `--pool=threads`, and the entry is gone. src/gate.mutation.test.ts holds the line.
